Fix $g\in G$ and write $H=C_G(g)$ for its centralizer.
For $k\ge0$ let $$\mathcal T_k(g)=H\backslash G^{k+1},$$ where $H$ acts by simultaneous left multiplication.
Let $n=2m>0$ and let $\alpha$ be a compatible connection family through dimension $n$.

Take $N=M_0r\epsilon^{-2}$ and define $$\begin{split}
 w^A_y&=\psi_A(E_r(P,y))^2
              e^{N(E_r(P,y)-0.80)},\\
 w^D_y&=\psi_D(E_r(P,y))^2
              e^{N(E_r(P,y)-0.66)},\\
 A(P)_y&=\frac{w^A_y}{1+\sum_z w^A_z},\qquad
 D(P)_y=\frac{w^D_y}{1+\sum_z w^D_z}.
 \end{split}
 \label{ch:selector-formulas}$$
Introduce a null symbol $\partial$, fixed by the group action, and the alphabet $$\mathcal A_z=B(z,20r)\cup\{\partial\}.$$

Now define a probability distribution on the entire fixed set of strings by $$\pi_z(P)_w
 =\frac{e^{-N_1S(P;z,w)}}{\sum_{v\in\mathcal A_z^b}e^{-N_1S(P;z,v)}},
 \qquad N_1=M_2rb\epsilon^{-2}.
 \label{ch:gibbs-strings}$$
Let $R$ be sufficiently large, choose the parameters in [co:ladder] and [co:last-scale], and let $n>10\beta_{b_*}$ be even, with time scales [co:time-scales].
Fix a sufficiently large $R$, and set $S=b_*+2$.
Let $\mu,\nu$ be finite nonatomic positive measures on $\mathbb R$, and set $M=\mu(\mathbb R)+\nu(\mathbb R)$.

Define the operator $T_j$ by the kernel $$T_j(u,y;v,z)
   =\sum_{a\in\mathbb Z}U_j(v+a-u)K_j(y,g^a z),

outputs.exact_statement:
Let $G$ be a discrete group, let $q\ge1$, and let $e\in M_q(\ell^1(G))$ be idempotent. There is a finite set $F\subset\mathcal C_{\rm fin}(G)$ such that $\tau_C(e)=0$ for every $C\notin F$. Equivalently, $$\operatorname{HS}^1\bigl(K_0(\ell^1(G))\bigr)
 \subseteq \bigoplus_{C\in\mathcal C_{\rm fin}(G)}\mathbb C[C].$$

For every conjugacy class $C$ of a discrete group $G$, the functional $$T_C(a)=\sum_{h\in C}\mathop{\mathrm{tr}}a(h),\qquad a\in M_q(\ell^1(G)),$$ is continuous and satisfies $T_C(ab)=T_C(ba)$. It is therefore invariant under similarity by invertible matrices over $\ell^1(G)$.

Let $e\in M_q(\ell^1(G))$ satisfy $e^2=e$. There are a finitely generated subgroup $\Gamma\le G$, a word length $|\cdot|$ on $\Gamma$, a number $c>0$, and an idempotent $p\in M_q(\ell^1(\Gamma))$ such that $$\label{red:exponential}
 \sum_{h\in\Gamma}|p(h)|_1e^{c|h|}<\infty,$$ and $p$ is similar to $e$ in $M_q(\ell^1(G))$. If the trace of every such $p$ has finite support on finite-order conjugacy classes of $\Gamma$, the same conclusion holds for every $e$ over every discrete group.

The following properties hold.*

1.  *The weights have total sum $\tau_{[g]}(p)$, in every dimension.*

2.  *Twisted rotation $(h_0,\ldots,h_k)\mapsto(h_1,\ldots,h_k,gh_0)$ preserves the weights.*

3.  *For $k\ge1$, summing the weights over all insertions of one entry into a fixed shortened tuple gives its weight in $\mathcal T_{k-1}(g)$.*


*All these sums converge absolutely, even after multiplication by any fixed polynomial in the edge lengths. In particular, with $M_p=\sum_{w\in G}|p(w)|_1(1+|w|)$, $$\label{cy:moment}
 \sum_{h\in\mathcal T_k(g)}|v_{k+1}(h)|\prod_{i=0}^k l_i
 \le M_p^{k+1}.$$

Let $n=2m>0$ and let $\alpha$ be a compatible connection family through dimension $n$. Write $A_h$ for the matrix of $d\alpha_h$ on the section $t_0=0$. If $\mathbb E_{\Delta_n}$ denotes uniform probability on $\Delta_n$, then $$\label{cy:trace-formula}
 \sum_{h\in\mathcal T_n(g)}v_{n+1}(h)\,
       \mathbb E_{\Delta_n}\mathop{\mathrm{Pf}}(A_h)
   =(-1)^m\tau_{[g]}(p).$$ The series converges absolutely.

Fix $r\ge1$ and $0<\epsilon\le10^{-3}$. There are channels $A,L$ and a cross kernel $\kappa$ with either of the following two choices of radius: the early version has $r'=6r$, and the later version has $r'=r$. In both versions $A$ is labelled by $G$, and for every $P\in\mathcal P_f(G)$ and $y\in G$, $$\begin{aligned} \sum_{z\in G}A(P)_z\bigl(E_r(P,z)-a_*\bigr) &\ge\phi_r(P)-10\epsilon, \label{ch:selection-bound}\\ \operatorname{pred}(P,y) &\le E_{r'}(P,y)+10\epsilon, \label{ch:prediction-upper}\\ \operatorname{pred}(P,y) &\ge E_r(P,y)-10\epsilon \qquad\text{if }A(P)_y>0. \label{ch:prediction-lower} \end{aligned}$$ For $Y=A$ or $Y=L$, derivatives in every transfer direction vanish at zero coordinates and satisfy $$\mathcal F_Y(P;h,h')\le C(1+d(h,h')) \begin{cases} \epsilon^{-10},&\text{early version},\\ r^{10}\epsilon^{-10},&\text{later version}. \end{cases} \label{ch:summary-fisher}$$ Here $C$ depends only on the fixed word metric. The numerical error constant $10$ in [ch:selection-bound]–[ch:prediction-lower] is independent of the group and of the parameters.
For $P\in\mathcal P_f(G)$, the set $\{y:E_r(P,y)>1/2\}$ has diameter at most $4r$ and cardinality at most $\exp(\gamma r)$, where $\gamma$ depends only on the word metric.

The formulas [ch:selector-formulas] define smooth equivariant channels. They satisfy $$\sum_y A(P)_y(E_r(P,y)-a_*)\ge\phi_r(P)-3\epsilon. \label{ch:selector-concentration}$$ Whenever $q_r(P)>0.70$, $$\sum_zD(P)_z\ge1-\epsilon, \qquad \sum_zD(P)_zE_r(P,z)\ge q_r(P)-2\epsilon. \label{ch:D-concentration}$$ Both channels have zero derivatives at zero coordinates, and $$\mathcal F_A(P;h,h')+\mathcal F_D(P;h,h') \le C\epsilon^{-2}d(h,h'). \label{ch:selector-fisher}$$

For each $r\ge1$ and $0<\epsilon\le10^{-3}$, the channel $D$ in [ch:selector-formulas] is smooth, left equivariant, and has total mass at most one. Its nonempty support has diameter at most $4r$ and cardinality at most $e^{\gamma r}$, with $\gamma$ depending only on the word metric. If $q_r(P)>0.70$, its mass is at least $1-\epsilon\ge1/2$. Its transfer derivatives vanish at zero coordinates and satisfy $$\mathcal F_D(P;h,h')\le C\epsilon^{-2}d(h,h') \le C\epsilon^{-10}(1+d(h,h')).$$ In particular, if $\phi_r(P)>0$, then $$\sum_zD(P)_z^2\ge\frac14e^{-\gamma r}. \label{ch:terminal-square-mass}$$

There is a constant $C$, depending only on the word metric, and an integer $b$ depending only on $r,\epsilon$, with $1\le b\le Cr\epsilon^{-4}$, such that for every $P$ and $z$ some $w\in\mathcal A_z^b$ satisfies $\Delta(P;z,w)\le\epsilon$.

The forms in [co:forms] are well defined, independent of the period cut, and smooth up to every simplex face by one-sided extension. They are invariant under simultaneous translation of all times, under the centralizer action, and under twisted rotation. Their tangential restrictions to faces equal the forms for the shortened tuples, using the same parameters and the same fixed integer $n$.

For every stage $0\leq j\leq b_*$, $$C_j:=B_j(V)
 =\int_{\rm per}\left(
 K_j(Y_j(u),Y_j(u))
 -\int_{\mathbb R}K_j(Y_j(u),Y_j(u+s))\,d\rho_j(s)\right)du.
 \label{co:contraction}$$ For $j<b_*$, the second integrated pairing is also $$\int_{\rm per}
 K_j\bigl((\mu_{j+1}*Y_j)(u),(\mu_{j+1}*Y_j)(u)\bigr)\,du.
 \label{co:averaged-pairing}$$

Under [co:twist-assumption], the scalar function $$C_{\rm nor}:=B(V)=\sum_{j=0}^{b_*-1}C_j+WC_{b_*} \label{co:normalizer}$$ satisfies $C_{\rm nor}\geq c_0$, where $c_0=1/10$ is independent of all tuples, $n$, $R$, and $g$.

Let $R$ be sufficiently large, choose the parameters in [co:ladder] and [co:last-scale], and let $n>10\beta_{b_*}$ be even, with time scales [co:time-scales]. Suppose that $g$ satisfies [co:twist-assumption]. The forms $B_j$ and $B$ in [co:forms], constructed in all dimensions $0\leq k\leq n$ with the same parameters, have the following properties. For every smooth stage $1\leq j\leq b_*$ and every coordinate $t_i$, $$\left(\int_{\rm per}\sum_\omega \frac{|\partial_iY_j(u)_\omega|^2}{Y_j(u)_\omega}\,du \right)^{1/2} \leq\frac{a_jl_i}{\sqrt{\delta_j}}. \label{co:fisher}$$ Terms with zero denominator are defined to be zero. Moreover, $$|B(\partial_i)|+|\partial_iC_{\rm nor}|\leq C_Rl_i. \label{co:coefficients}$$ The scalar $C_{\rm nor}$ is at least $c_0=1/10$, and $$\alpha=\frac{B}{C_{\rm nor}} \label{co:normalized}$$ is a compatible connection family in the sense of Definition 5. Its coefficients and those of its exterior derivative are bounded by polynomials in the lengths, uniformly over the tuples. In particular, the family may be used in Proposition 6.

Fix a sufficiently large $R$, and set $S=b_*+2$. Let $n$ be an even integer with $n>10\beta_{b_*}$. Suppose either that $g$ has infinite order, or that $g$ has finite order and $$\min_{h\in G}d(h,gh)>4r.$$ For every tuple $(h_0,\ldots,h_n)$, the connection $\alpha=B/C_{\rm nor}$ of Proposition 17 satisfies $$\mathbb E_{\Delta_n}|\mathop{\mathrm{Pf}}(d\alpha)| \le C_R\bigl(CS^{3/2}R^{-1/10}\bigr)^n \prod_{i=1}^n l_i, \qquad l_i=1+d(h_{i-1},h_i). \label{pf:main-estimate}$$ The constants are independent of $n,g$, and the tuple. Moreover, $S=O(1+\log R)$ as $R\to\infty$.

Let $\mu,
u$ be finite nonatomic positive measures on $\mathbb R$, and set $M=\mu(\mathbb R)+
u(\mathbb R)$. Let $A:L^2(
u)	o L^2(\mu)$ have any one of the kernels $$\operatorname{sign}(s-t),\qquad
 \mathbf1_{s<t},\qquad \mathbf1_{s>t},$$ where $t$ is the output variable and $s$ the input variable. For each integer $N\ge1$, there is an operator $A_N$ of rank at most $N$ such that $$\|A-A_N\|\le  rac{M}{2N}.$$ Also $\|A\|\le\sqrt{\mu(\mathbb R)
u(\mathbb R)}\le M/2$.

For the operator $T_{b_*}$, every finite-dimensional orthogonal compression has singular values satisfying $$s_ u\le rac C u,\qquad u\ge1. \label{pf:singular-decay}$$ The constant is independent of $n,R,g$, and the tuple, in either of the two cases of Theorem 18.
